answer: Give every new identity a mirrored work history: before it can take paid work, it must complete small public tasks whose outputs are mirrored by two unrelated peers and stored in an open audit trail, like timber beams checked from both sides. A Sybil attacker who clones identities must redo that slow, peer-checked work for each copy and post a separate refundable bond per identity, so creating a karst of hollow shells costs real time and capital while gaining no trust, and any mirror mismatch burns the bond and exposes the whole cluster.
